body.text: Start time (date -u): 2026-11-04T03:45:00Z. Hard stop: 2026-11-04T11:45:00Z. I will reconstruct the single right-hand demonstration, record validation and limitations, define independent simulation verification criteria, build a physically actuated Wuji Hand 2.2 simulation, and train deployable closed-loop PPO policies. Reconstruction has its own 60-minute budget; incomplete or failed components will be recorded as an exception, never described as VALID.

Elapsed about 11 minutes of 8 hours. Initial silhouette tracking gave implausible charger orientations and large depth drift at rest. I replaced it with support-constrained fitting and a shared camera estimated from background rotation plus resting-object anchors. Object-only median silhouette IoU is now 0.870 white and 0.784 black; unsupported hidden poses remain invalid. Hypothesis: a demonstration-derived wrist/fingertip reference with a deployable PPO residual can bridge hand morphology while preserving the observed palm-down approach and wrist reorientation. Baseline performance must be measured separately; no scripted baseline will be reported as a learned solution.

The reconstruction currently passes check_reference.py format validation, but independent validation fails finger self-intersection (48.9% of valid frames), and opposing-thumb contact is weak (10.2% white, 8.2% black). I will not describe this as a successful quality reconstruction. The provided default MANO fit has no self-collision or mandatory opposing-finger loss, so I copied it into research/handlib_extended and added distal-finger capsule separation plus explicit thumb/opposing-finger surface-distance losses. Installed tools and hardware/object specifications remain unchanged. I will validate the modified fit and disclose its effect on silhouette agreement and anatomical contacts. PPO reference: Schulman et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347; planned RL uses only its clipped-surrogate PPO family.

body.summary: Shared metric reconstruction of the two sequential charger pickups: Blender known-dimension bodies/blades, support-constrained silhouette poses, background/standing-object camera anchors, HaWoR-initialized MANO fitting extended in workspace copy for opposed contact and finger separation. check_reference VALID; independent validation overall PASS with self-intersection warning.

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

body.text: Reconstruction version 1 is recorded as r0004 at 04:08:27 UTC, within the 60-minute reconstruction budget (23.5 minutes elapsed). Format VALID, independent validation overall PASS; one residual finger intersection frame (396; fraction .003) remains a warning. Opposed-grasp fractions are .810 white and .985 black. Criteria v1 is now fixed before policy evaluation. Next: build the exact-mass, torque-limited floating-wrist Wuji simulation from the provided URDF, retarget the recorded wrist/palm and object phases, validate controllers and contact support, then train deployable PPO. About 7 h 36 min remain.

scene.robot: Public Wuji Hand 2.2 right URDF; exact joint frames, link masses/inertias, armatures and effort limits. Original STL visuals; fitted primitive collision shapes. Mechanical-neighbor collisions excluded, cross-finger collision enabled.
scene.objects: Sharp collision boxes with fixed blade boxes; body COM +2mm bladeward; white .075kg, black .055kg; supplied dimensions; inferred inertias.
scene.table: 1.2 x 1.2 x .03 m centered (.1,0,-.015), floor z=-.75; +Y left, +Z up.

reference.method: Offline kinematic retargeting of diagonal thumb/index body contacts with pad normals, full-link surface nonpenetration, conservative table clearances and wrist orientation adaptation within 25deg of reconstructed palm. Shortest 90deg blade-axis reorientation removes ambiguous reconstructed axial spin. This unlearned baseline is not a reported PPO solution.
reference.adaptation: Offline pad-position and normal IK, full-link nonpenetration and table clearance. Human palm axes mapped to robot root. Ambiguous object axial spin removed while preserving start/end blade axis and measured translations. This is an unlearned reference baseline.

controllers.wrist: Hardware wrist-1 at 1kHz, hand-only gravity compensation, 2000/60 translation,20/.4 rotation,30N and2Nm norm caps. Commands 500Hz,2.5m/s and6rad/s target caps.
controllers.fingers: Specified 1kHz joint PD gains and torque saturation; joint target clipping; no joint state/velocity clipping. Every actual 1kHz velocity checked; terminate on violation.
controllers.policy: 50Hz residual network produces 26 actions; pose/finger targets interpolated to 500Hz. Position residual .015m, rotation-vector residual .18rad, finger residual .18rad per action unit; EMA command weight .35; finger target rate1.5rad/s. Only reference preprocessing, no runtime optimization.

initial_conditions.reason: The first supported reconstructed approach (frame37), adapted to larger hand morphology; object poses from frame0 under a single rigid frame offset.

episode.termination: 16s, any hardware position/speed violation, object falling below table, invalid actions

validation.wrist_controller: 2000/60 N/m translational, 20/.4 rotational, hand-only gravity compensation, 30N and 2Nm norm saturation. Direct forces applied at wrist root using mj_applyFT.
limitations: No torque-speed envelope published; measured velocities are checked against max speeds every tick, with termination on any violation rather than hidden clipping.

Hand collision shapes are fitted boxes/capsules/ellipsoids with original mesh visuals, masses and inertias. Adjacent mechanical assemblies have collision exclusions to avoid false convex-hull contacts. This approximates the true contact surfaces and pad compliance.
Reference retargeting is kinematic and not a learned controller. Its dynamic baseline is separately evaluated.

unlearned_baseline.diagnosis: Thumb touches first; index remains too far; object slides rather than lifts. No demonstrated grasp/lift/placement; later hardware speed violation. Baseline is not a learned PPO solution.

body.text: Simulation v1 recorded as r0007 at 04:29:54 UTC, after reconstruction r0004 and criteria r0005. Starting iteration 1: deployable 111-input, 26-output residual PPO, separate 128x128 tanh actor/critic, 16 randomized CPU MuJoCo environments, clipped surrogate .2, gamma .995, GAE .95, actor learning rate .0003. Unlearned reference baseline fails: no opposed grasp/lift, thumb pushes white, later joint-speed violation. Hypothesis: dense pad-proximity and opposed-force shaping plus object-state feedback can learn earlier index closure and correct the morphology/contact gap. Training capped at 800000 transitions or 30 minutes; then full recorded criteria evaluation, videos and diagnosis. Elapsed 46 minutes; hard stop remains 11:45 UTC.
